The central claim MUST be graded on the evidence found, not 'not checkable here': web_fetch the release or report that published its figures and grade on it; when that page will not load, grade on copies that quote it. 'not checkable here' is only for a personal attack or a claim that is an opinion or belief no evidence can test ('chocolate chip cookies are the best cookies'), marked kind: opinion, with a reason saying in one sentence why no evidence can test it (an opinion of taste, a belief, or figurative speech); a missing table or a page that will not load never makes a factual claim uncheckable; when nothing found supports it, it is 'unsupported'. For an opinion that may imply a checkable fact ('politician A is a crook'), the claim's reason MUST state whether the speaker meant it literally, from the context. Meant literally ('has committed crimes'), the implied fact MUST be split out as its own claim, searched for (a criminal record) and graded; meant figuratively ('is dishonest'), it stays an opinion. 7. A figure the piece presents as a projection or early estimate MUST be graded on whether it matches the estimate the agency published, or the arithmetic of the components the agency published.
